Andrey Vladimirovich Vasnetsov (Russian: Андре́й Влади́мирович Васнецо́в; 24 February 1924 – 6 December 2009) was a Soviet and Russian painter and art educator. He was an important figure in the Moscow art scene of the post-Stalin era and one of the founders of the Severe Style (Russian: surovy stil), a major current in Soviet art from the late 1950s. In 1962 his painting Breakfast was among the works denounced by Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev during his visit to the "30 Years of the Moscow Union of Artists" exhibition at the Moscow Manege.
